sam: heads-up — saw sustained mem growth on mistral long-context CI runs, KV page count climbs linearly over 2h, throughput drops ~12% :grimacing:
denise: ugh, is this the rope-scaling case again? any repro steps or traces? :thinking:
sam: reproducer attached below, quick run with long prefix (40k) + batching=continuous. logs show repeated `kernel fallback -> mmapped pager` and `kv_pages_alloc=...` spikes
sam: ```
$ ./run_infer --model mistral-xl-32k --seq 40000 --batching continuous --trace kvcache --out /tmp/mistral-kv.log
KV pages: 23456 -> 28901 (+ 4.2k every 10m)
kernel: voted_mmap=true fallback_reason=slot_frag
```
aj: can you paste the flamegraph link? I want to see if kernel selection hotpaths line up with the paging spikes
sam: https://perf.redwood.internal/graphs/3487654321-mistral-kv-longprefix (private) — top of stack is `kv_reuse_policy::try_retain_prefix` then `kernel_selector::choose_fallback`
maria: interesting — on Qwen we saw similar linear growth but it stabilized after we adjusted the batching heuristic (max_batch_time -> 8ms). maybe batching keeps short kernels pinned and prevents KV coalescing
denise: are you using GQA vs MQA variant for this run? rope scaling interacts with slot allocation differently depending on query vs model attention quantization
sam: Mistral-run is MQA. Qwen tests were GQA. differences: MQA allocate slightly larger slot footprints for same seq length, which looks like it fragments slabs earlier
perf-bot: [alert] CI perf-regression: mistral-xl-32k longseq throughput -11.8% (compare branch:main -> branch:mst-fix)
aj: can we try forcing kernel selection to prefer compact kernels? quick A/B: `KERNEL_PREFERENCE=compact ./run_infer ...` should avoid fallback to mmap path
sam: tried that, less paging but tail latency increased by 30ms — looks like compact kernel has worse KV locality for these ropes
maria: maybe try disabling prefix caching for a run: `KV_PREFIX_CACHE=0` — that will stress eviction/repick logic and show if reuse policy is the culprit
sam: will run both flags now, posting logs in ~15m :eyes:
infra-bot: note: large runs on dedicated qemu nodes may trigger host-level swapping if mmap thrash occurs — check node /var/log/kern.log for OOM/kpage warnings
denise: if swapping at host observed, reduce concurrency on the job and retest, because mmap-backed pages are vulnerable to host reclaim
sam: quick summary after two runs:
 - KERNEL_PREFERENCE=compact: kv_page_growth slowed, total pages -8%, but p95 latency +32ms
 - KV_PREFIX_CACHE=0: pages still grow, but fragmentation pattern changed (smaller live runs with more small free slots)
 - kernel fallback messages still present, mostly at long prefix lengths > 30k
aj: sounds like a mixed cause: batching heuristic + MQA slot size + kernel fallback heuristics. next actions: 1) add a telemetry counter for `kv_fragmentation_ratio` per model-variant, 2) run long-prefix simbench with deterministic rope scale to reproduce, 3) try a patch to kernel_selector to bias against mmap fallback when fragmentation_ratio < 0.2
denise: +1 on telemetry. add a quick synthetic test in ci/perf that runs 45k prefix on both GQA/MQA variants so we catch regressions earlier
maria: I'll draft a microbenchmark and a quick experiment toggling `max_batch_time` policy; also will sanity-check allocator slab size thresholds for MQA
sam: thanks — will open a short PR with the repro scripts + logs and tag you all. marking as follow-up in the thread. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: [note] created perf issue #PLAT-8421 linked to this thread
infra-bot: reminder: if you need retained traces, push to /s3/perf-retention/mistral/kvcache/3487654321
aj: nice writeup, thanks. if we can get deterministic simbench reproducer we can try a few eviction algos (LRU vs clock-probabilistic) to measure fragmentation impact
denise: assigning to sam+mar iaw — let's reconvene once PR + telemetry land
sam: will do, thanks everyone!
